messages:
Incident Bot: [PAGE] KV cache prefix hit-rate collapse for tenant orchid-labs in dedicated pool dp-14 (VPC vpc-east-1b). 5m window: prefix hit-rate dropped 82% -> 4%. p95 token latency up ~6x. Severity: P1. Pager triggered to infra-oncall.

Mike Chen: ACKed. Paging infra oncall. @Ravi can you take?

Ravi Kumar: taking. pulling metrics and recent access patterns. I see a sudden spike in unique prefix cardinality starting at 10:04 UTC with many TTL=0 writes. likely tenant-driven churn (cache pollution).

Laura Patel: confirm isolation impact — are other tenants on dp-14 affected?

Ravi Kumar: quick roll-up: dp-14 other tenants stable. this is isolated to orchid-labs. network and node health checks OK. suspect a batch job or rollout from customer.

Tess Müller: can we put an emergency soft-partition on that tenant's cache so their noisy prefixes stop evicting global hot prefixes? we have a toggle for per-tenant partitioning.

Ravi Kumar: plan to: 1) enable soft per-tenant partitioning (10m) 2) build eviction list of top noisy prefixes and evict 3) temporarily enforce min-TTL for that tenant 4) scale prefetch workers to warm cache. Executing step 1 now.

Ravi Kumar: admin API call:
```
POST /admin/v1/dedicated/dp-14/tenants/orchid-labs/cache/partition
{"mode":"soft","duration_sec":600}
```
API -> 202 Accepted. Applying eviction query to KV-access logs.

Ravi Kumar: eviction selection query (ran against clickhouse):
```
SELECT prefix, count() AS cnt, uniqExact(src_id) AS callers FROM kv_access
WHERE tenant='orchid-labs' AND ts > now() - INTERVAL 10 MINUTE
GROUP BY prefix ORDER BY cnt DESC LIMIT 100
```
Evicting top 100 noisy prefixes now.

Incident Bot: [ACTION] soft-partition applied, eviction job queued, prefetch workers +4 for tenant orchid-labs.

Ana Rivera: CS update sent to customer at 10:22 UTC — told them we're applying targeted mitigations and will follow up. Customer devlead said they started a data backfill at ~10:03 which may match the window.

Ravi Kumar: post-eviction metrics: tenant prefix hit-rate climbed from 4% -> 42% within 3 minutes. p95 token latency improved 1.8s -> 470ms. still above baseline but trending. keeping TTL-floor and partition for now.

Mike Chen: suppress noisy alerts for orchid-labs for 20m to avoid duplicate pages while we monitor. Also ask for heap/profile dumps from cache nodes for root-cause analysis.

Ravi Kumar: captured heap + perf profiles off dp-14 cache nodes and uploaded to debug bucket: s3://redwood-debug/1886001234-orchid-cache-profiles. Attached recent logs to INC-1886001234.

Tess Müller: can the product/infra team add a guardrail to reject TTL=0 writes coming from VPC tenants or at least rate-limit them? TTL=0 spam is too easy to trigger.

Ravi Kumar: temporary measure applied: enforce tenant min_ttl=30s override for orchid-labs for 15m. Command:
```
PATCH /admin/v1/tenants/orchid-labs/cache/ttl-override
{"min_ttl_seconds":30,"duration_sec":900}
```
Response 200.

Mike Chen: good. CS asked customer to throttle their backfill and namespace prefixes. They agreed to patch their job. Ana, please confirm once they push a fix.

Ana Rivera: customer confirmed they'll change the job to batch by stable prefixes and set TTLs. They requested a short postmortem and engineer contact for follow-up.

Ravi Kumar: monitoring update: at 10:48 UTC hit-rate ~71%, p95 token latency ~200ms. Removing soft partition and TTL-floor in 10m if stable. Leaving investigation and follow-ups in ticket.

Laura Patel: assigning postmortem owner. I'll draft timeline, include metrics, commands run, and remediation suggestions (automation: detect high prefix cardinality per tenant and auto-surface noisy prefixes).

Mike Chen: handoff to Tess for afternoon oncall. I'll remain on slack for CS comms. Tess, you're primary for final verification and rollback decisions.

Tess Müller: taking handoff. will validate at 11:05 UTC and confirm. noted follow-ups: CS-ENG runbook update, INF-guardrail task, and product visibility for tenant metrics.

Incident Bot: Incident state -> mitigated. Severity downgraded to P2 at 10:50 UTC. Next automated check at 11:05 UTC.

Ravi Kumar: final check 11:04 UTC: hit-rate steady 75%, p95 165ms. closing active page, leaving monitoring. Follow-ups filed: SOL-102 (customer patch verification), INF-420 (TTL guardrail), DOCS-31 (runbook).

Laura Patel: postmortem draft ETA EOD. Will include customer comms and recommended automation thresholds.

Incident Bot: Incident resolved -> cleared at 11:15 UTC. Please confirm any outstanding owners in INC-1886001234.
